findings: Source-assisted: Compass 2/5, Graphify 0/5. This includes resolver and CLI-ID interoperability; it is not a pure path-algorithm score.

Native short labels: tie at 1/5. Both return a source-supported six-call Click route. Compass selects text stdout/writer; Graphify selects text stdin/reader, independently source-reviewed after capture and accepted. It is not a preregistered occurrence match.
Compass source-assisted Chi returns six calls, using another valid InsertRoute-to-addChild occurrence at tree.go:234 instead of the frozen :183.

Compass jsoup returns a four-edge instantiates/contains/contains/calls route and marks the depth-8 search truncated. WalkDir returns a three-edge calls/returns/contains route. Neither is a call-chain answer.

The post-capture private-graph calls-only diagnostic finds all registered Compass call steps for Chi, Click, jsoup and WalkDir. This separates existing edge availability from public route selection; it is not credited as a public answer.
Neither tool exposes Redux combination at the frozen named-function-expression coordinate. The graph diagnostic keeps this missing endpoint, rather than selecting combineReducers as a substitute.

Graphify source-assisted Chi silently uses different endpoints, jsoup IDs resolve to the same unintended node and fail, and WalkDir next lookup fails the frozen source coordinate. Native labels are published separately rather than choosing the best arm per case.

Eighteen Compass depth probes produce thirteen explicitly bounded empty results, four mixed routes and one valid Click route at depth six. No empty bounded result claims complete absence. Reverse probes receive no source-global absence credit.
